admission.justification: A code-only digest and a resource-inclusive digest were both drafted and weighed; the choice binds every later change to the currentness comparison.

alternatives.option: Digest only the Python source files of the package; a Markdown-only install adds no stale mark and no write refusal.
alternatives.reason: The developer kept the check on code. A refusal triggered by instruction text alone would be a new guard without a repeated failure behind it, and a new guard needs his acceptance.

alternatives.option: Extend the same digest to served and compiled resources (role and operation Markdown, package data, additions and removals), so a Markdown-only change marks a running installed server stale.
alternatives.reason: Rejected by the developer with the review-born proofs that came with it; no repeated failure justified a new refusing guard.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Running servers that serve outdated instruction text after an install become a repeated failure and the developer accepts a resource-inclusive guard.

consequences: A server whose Python matches the installed build reports current even when its served instruction text is older; reconnecting loads the new text.
The separate catalog refusal of resources changed since catalog construction stays the protection for served bytes.
context: After an install a running MCP server or dashboard keeps the build it loaded. The loaded-versus-installed comparison needs a population to digest. One draft widened it from the Python code to every resource the server serves or compiles, so that a change of role or operation Markdown alone would mark a running installed server stale and make it refuse publications.
decider: The developer (D640 Q11, under D518: a new guard needs a repeating issue and his acceptance); MIK-R84 v4 amendment 1.
